snip.t: Valproate is a category X drug that is associated with neural tube defects, hypospadias, and cardiovascular malformationsand should be avoided if possible during pregnancy.
The most common genitourinary anomalies associated with Wilms tumor are hypoplasia, fusion and ectopia of the kidney, duplications of the collecting systems, hypospadias, and cryptorchidism
• In hypospadias the opening is towards the scrotum or ventral\nside

Penis: foreskin (phimosis, paraphimosis, balanitis, balanitis xerotica obliterans/lichen sclerosus), the external meatus (hypospadias, meatal stenosis, discharge), the shaft (plaques of Peyronie's, lesions), and the glans (cancer).

snip.t: Risk factors: cryptorchidism (3 to 8 times; the risk persists after orchidopexy), a family history (father or brother), a previous testicular cancer (contralateral), infertility, HIV, hypospadias, carcinoma in situ, in-utero exposure (DES), and Klinefelter's syndrome.

Iatrogenic: instrumentation (urethral catheters, especially prolonged indwelling and large catheters, cystoscopy, passing sounds), surgery (TURP and prostatectomy, hypospadias repair), and radiotherapy.

snip.t: Associated conditions: hypospadias, patent processus vaginalis (inguinal hernia), abdominal wall defects (prune belly, gastroschisis, omphalocele), cerebral palsy, Wilms tumour, syndromes such as Klinefelter's, and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism.

qs.q: An 8-month-old boy is evaluated for bilateral cryptorchidism and is noted to have associated hypospadias and ambiguous genitalia. Which initial investigations should be ordered urgently?
o: Bilateral scrotal ultrasound and serum alpha-fetoprotein
Karyotype, 17-hydroxyprogesterone, electrolytes, testosterone, LH, and FSH
Intravenous urogram and baseline serum creatinine
Diagnostic laparoscopy and pelvic magnetic resonance imaging
qs.e: Bilateral impalpable testes with hypospadias or ambiguous genitalia suggest a disorder of sex development or congenital adrenal hyperplasia requiring urgent workup including 17-hydroxyprogesterone and karyotype. Scrutiny by ultrasound is of limited diagnostic value for locating testes compared to surgical exploration.

qs.q: A 9-month-old boy is evaluated in the surgical clinic for bilateral impalpable testes. Physical examination additionally reveals penoscrotal hypospadias and ambiguous genitalia. What is the most critical underlying diagnosis that must be investigated?
o: Assess for congenital adrenal hyperplasia and related intersex conditions
Investigate Kallmann syndrome associated with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
Consider isolated bilateral vanishing testis (anorchia) syndrome
Evaluate for prune‑belly syndrome with possible renal agenesis
qs.e: Bilateral impalpable testes accompanied by hypospadias strongly indicate an intersex state and congenital adrenal hyperplasia. Vanishing testis syndrome does not present with hypospadias or ambiguous genitalia.

qs.q: How is hypospadias anatomically distinguished from epispadias regarding the location of the urethral opening?
o: Hypospadias has a duplicated meatus, whereas epispadias is closed
Hypospadias is dorsal, whereas epispadias is within the scrotum
Hypospadias opens at the umbilicus, whereas epispadias is perineal
Hypospadias opens ventrally, whereas epispadias opens dorsally
qs.e: In hypospadias, the opening is towards the ventral side or scrotum, whereas in epispadias, the opening is towards the abdomen or dorsal surface of the penis. Both represent abnormal positions of the external urethral meatus.

qs.q: Why is circumcision strictly contraindicated in a newborn infant diagnosed with hypospadias?
o: Circumcision increases the baseline incidence of reflux
The dorsal prepuce skin is needed for later surgical repair
It interferes with the healing of underlying prune belly
It causes immediate closure of the ectopic external meatus
qs.e: Circumcision is an absolute contraindication in hypospadias because the dorsal urethral skin is required for reconstructive repair later on, particularly in proximal hypospadias. Repair is typically undertaken at 6 to 9 months of age.
